sections.overview: This large Mediterranean spider belongs to Segestriidae.
sections.identification: Adults are dark; chelicerae may shine green or bronze.
sections.habitat: It shelters in tree hollows, crevices, walls and buildings.
sections.diet: Prey include beetles, moths, wasps, woodlice and spiders.
sections.behavior: It waits in a tubular retreat on radiating signal threads, then strikes passing prey.
sections.reproduction: The female guards her autumn egg sac and young.
sections.ecology: The World Spider Catalog records it from Europe and North Africa east to Georgia, and as introduced in parts of South America.
sections.conservation: The French INPN account lists the species as Least Concern in France; this is a national assessment.
